content.title: Key Takeaways
items: AI Visibility is not something a law firm can simply "turn on" — it's the ongoing result of making the firm's information clear, consistent, trustworthy, structured, and easy to verify.

No firm, tool, or checklist can guarantee that any AI system will recommend, cite, rank, or display a law firm — AI systems control their own retrieval and ranking mechanisms, which are outside any individual firm's control.
This checklist evaluates 18 categories, from business identity to technical discoverability, and should be worked through using observable evidence, not assumptions about what "probably" exists.

Structured data, FAQ content, and consistent local information can all help make a firm's information easier to understand — none of them, individually or combined, guarantees a specific visibility outcome.

Google fully deprecated FAQ rich search results as of May 2026, after restricting them since 2023 — a reminder that specific technical tactics change over time, while clear, accurate, well-organized content remains the durable foundation.
The practical sequence for using this checklist is: audit, identify gaps, prioritize, improve, verify, and re-audit — this is a recurring discipline, not a one-time project.

content.content: Prospective clients increasingly research a law firm through more than a single channel — search engines, Google Maps, legal directories, reviews, the firm's own website, and a growing layer of AI-powered search tools and conversational assistants that summarize information directly rather than presenting a list of links to click through.

A firm can be genuinely excellent at law and still be difficult to understand from the outside: an inconsistent business name across directories, a practice-area page that says almost nothing, attorney information that's years out of date, or FAQ content that never actually addresses what a worried prospective client wants to know. None of these problems reflect a lack of legal skill — they reflect a gap in how clearly that skill is communicated.

content.title: No Outcome Guarantees
content.content: This checklist is built to help close that gap. It can tell a firm where its information is clear, consistent, and well-supported, and where it's thin, contradictory, or simply missing. It cannot tell a firm that completing every item will produce a specific search ranking, an AI citation, or a new client — no honest resource can promise that.

content.title: 2. What Is AI Visibility for a Law Firm?

content.content: For the purposes of this checklist, AI Visibility means: the degree to which a law firm's publicly available information is clear, consistent, useful, structured, trustworthy, and discoverable enough for search engines and AI-powered systems to potentially understand the firm correctly.

content.title: 7 Foundational Questions for Law Firm AI Visibility

items.definition: Official firm name, entity structure, and brand clarity.
Specific practice areas and clear legal service scope.
Physical office location and explicitly defined service area.
Specific legal situations and client concerns handled.

items.term: What topics do you have expertise in?
items.definition: Depth of educational and practice-area content.
Bar credentials, directory consistency, and authoritative citations.

items: PASS — this is clearly and verifiably in place
PARTIAL — this exists but has meaningful gaps or inconsistencies
FAIL — this is missing or clearly incorrect
N/A — not applicable to this firm's specific situation

content.title: Evidence Over Assumptions
content.content:
One rule matters more than any other in this entire process: do not mark an item "Pass" because the firm assumes it's true. A checklist item should be supported by observable evidence, not a general impression.

Bad: "We probably have this."
Good: "The firm's official website, at [specific page], clearly displays this information, confirmed on [date]."

content.title: 2026 FAQPage Structured Data Deprecation Notice
content.content: Google fully deprecated FAQ rich search results as of May 2026, after restricting them since 2023. FAQPage markup remains technically valid schema.org, but it no longer produces visible rich results in search. Retain it if helpful for machine readability, but do not rely on it for rich snippet visibility.

content.content: The complete master checklist aggregates all 18 categories above into a unified audit document for comprehensive law firm review.

items: High Readiness — large majority score PASS; clear, consistent, well-maintained information.
Moderate Readiness — mix of PASS and PARTIAL items; solid foundation with room for improvement.
Needs Improvement — significant PARTIAL/FAIL items; core information gaps affect clarity.
Foundational Gaps — majority of FAIL items in core categories (Business Identity, Location, Practice Areas).

rows: High impact, addresses foundational gap or inconsistency
Incorrect phone number across directories; missing practice page
Thin FAQ coverage for a core practice area
Adding glossary entries for less common terms
Polishing internal linking on low-traffic page

content.title: AI Prompt Template: Law Firm AI Visibility Audit Assistant
content.prompt:
You are helping a law firm audit its publicly available online information using Locatria's AI Visibility Checklist framework.

FIRM INFORMATION:
Firm Name:
Website:
City / Service Area:
Practice Areas:
Attorney Information (names, roles, as publicly listed):
Google Business Profile Information:
Major Legal Directory Information:
Key Website Pages:
Structured Data Status, if known:
Review / Reputation Notes:
Other Relevant Public Information:

Please review this information and produce an audit that:
- Organizes findings by category
- Identifies inconsistencies across the sources provided
- Clearly distinguishes confirmed facts from assumptions
- Identifies missing information across each category
- Identifies unclear or thin practice-area descriptions
- Identifies location-related gaps
- Identifies FAQ and educational content opportunities
- Identifies trust and credibility gaps
- Identifies technical questions requiring human/SEO review
- Prioritizes improvements as P1 (Critical), P2 (High), P3 (Medium), or P4 (Later)
- Flags any item requiring professional or attorney verification

Important instructions:
- Use only the information supplied above; do not invent facts.
- Clearly distinguish evidence from assumption throughout your response.
- Do not provide legal advice or make legal conclusions.
- Do not request or process any confidential client information.
- Do not claim that fixing these issues guarantees search rankings or AI citations.
- Do not invent citations or fabricate evidence for any finding.

content.title: 32. What the Checklist Can and Cannot Do

pros: Establish a baseline understanding of information ecosystem
cons: Cannot guarantee leads, clients, or revenue
Cannot predict exact behavior of specific AI systems

items.question: What is AI Visibility for a law firm?
items.answer: AI Visibility is the degree to which a law firm's publicly available information is clear, consistent, useful, structured, trustworthy, and discoverable enough for search engines and AI-powered systems to potentially understand the firm correctly.

items.question: How can a law firm audit its AI Visibility?
items.answer: Work through the eighteen categories in this checklist using observable evidence rather than assumptions, mark each item PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, or N/A, record where the evidence came from, and use the scorecard and prioritization matrix to decide what to fix first.

items.question: Does AI Visibility replace local SEO?
items.answer: No. AI Visibility builds on the same fundamentals local SEO already established — accurate business information, consistent local signals, useful content — and extends them to a broader set of AI-powered discovery experiences.

items.question: Can a law firm guarantee ChatGPT visibility?
items.answer: No. No firm, tool, or technique can guarantee that any specific AI system will cite, recommend, or display a particular law firm. AI systems control their own retrieval and ranking mechanisms, which are not something any individual business can fully control.

items.question: Can this checklist guarantee AI recommendations?
items.answer: No. This checklist evaluates information clarity, consistency, and completeness — factors within a firm's control. It cannot guarantee how any AI system will ultimately behave.

items.question: What information should a law firm make clear online?
items.answer: At minimum: the firm's name, location and service area, practice areas, attorney information, and how a prospective client can verify all of it — consistently, across the firm's own website and every external source.

items.question: How important is location information?
items.answer: Very important. Location and service-area clarity are foundational to both local search and general understanding of who the firm can actually help.

items.question: Do practice-area pages matter for AI visibility?
items.answer: Yes. Clear, specific, well-organized practice-area pages help both visitors and systems understand exactly what the firm handles.

items.question: Should law firms create FAQ content?
items.answer: Yes, when it reflects genuinely recurring client questions and stays appropriately general and educational. FAQ content is valuable for clarity and usefulness even though, as of 2026, it no longer produces visible rich results in Google Search.

items.question: Does structured data guarantee AI visibility?
items.answer: No. Structured data can help systems parse already-accurate information more precisely, but it does not guarantee inclusion in any specific search feature or AI answer.

items.question: How often should a law firm perform an AI Visibility audit?
items.answer: At minimum on a recurring schedule — quarterly is a reasonable starting point — and immediately after any significant change: a new attorney, a new practice area, a relocation, or a substantial website update.

items.question: Can AI perform the audit automatically?
items.answer: AI can help organize, compare, and classify information quickly using a prompt like the one in this guide, but a person must verify every finding, confirm legal accuracy, and make final decisions.

items.question: Should confidential client information be used in an AI audit?
items.answer: No. Visibility audits should rely entirely on public information — the firm's own public website, public business profiles, and public directory listings.

items.question: How should a law firm prioritize AI Visibility improvements?
items.answer: Use the Impact/Effort/Risk framework: address critical, foundational gaps first, then move to high-value improvements, and save minor refinements for later.

items.question: What should a law firm fix first?
items.answer: Foundational information problems — inconsistent business identity, unclear location information, and missing or incomplete practice-area content — should be addressed before more advanced tactics.
